info.title: Testing changes with a shadow configuration

abstract.para: You can use a shadow configuration to test different configuration scenarios. If you create multiple shadow configurations, you can test them one by one to see the effects of your changes.

topic.para: This example procedure shows the process for creating and using a shadow configuration:

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.

step.screen: &prompt.crm.conf;cib new test1 INFO: configure.cib.new: test1 shadow CIB created crm(test1)configure#
step.para: The prompt changes from live to the name of the shadow configuration. If you don't specify a name, the temporary name @tmp@ is used instead.
Make the changes you want to test. These changes will only apply to the shadow configuration, not to the live configuration.
Save the changes to see their effect on the cluster:
Switch back to the live configuration:
The prompt changes back to live.
You can switch back to the shadow configuration if you need to use it again later:
To undo the changes in the shadow configuration, or to update the shadow configuration to match the latest live configuration, you can run the following command:
step.screen: crm(test1)configure# cib reset test1 INFO: configure.cib.reset: copied live CIB to test1
